title: Read The Weak-Side Tag
description: Spot the low-man tag on a spread pick-and-roll and make the simple kickout before the defense recovers.
takeaway: Read the tag early and punish the helper, not the primary defender.

annotations.title: Tag forms
annotations.note: The weak-side defender steps in before the roller catches.

annotations.title: Window opens
annotations.note: The skip pass is cleaner than forcing a pocket pass through traffic.

annotations.title: Punish the help
annotations.note: Early recognition turns a crowded paint into a catch-and-shoot three.

answer_key: The right read is the kickout because the low man has tagged the roller.

title: Beat The Nail Help
description: Learn how to attack middle drives when the nail defender stunts and recovers.
takeaway: Change pace before you change direction.
answer_key: Reject the stunt, keep the dribble alive, and attack the recovering foot.

pause_predict.prompt: The nail defender shows early. What is the best next action?

choices.label: Pick up the dribble and throw a late skip pass
Change pace, keep the live dribble, and re-attack the stunt foot
Force a contested floater over two bodies

pause_predict.explanation: A live dribble keeps both passing and finishing options open while the helper is still off-balance.

learn_more.title: Why the nail matters
learn_more.body: Elite defenses shrink the floor from the nail because it disrupts straight-line drives without fully rotating.

title: Attack Closeouts Without Overdribbling
description: Turn scrambled closeouts into paint touches while staying on schedule with the offense.
takeaway: One advantage dribble is often enough.
answer_key: Rip through the top foot, collapse help, then move the ball.

scenario.prompt: You catch on the wing with a hard closeout and a rim protector waiting. Which process is best?

options.title: Take three hard dribbles into traffic
options.description: You attack downhill immediately and try to finish through two extra defenders.

options.title: Take one advantage dribble, force a second helper, and make the next pass
options.description: You use the closeout against the defense without holding the ball too long.

options.title: Reset the possession even though the defense is tilted
options.description: You avoid the risk but also give away the advantage.

scenario.explanation: The closeout already created an edge. Preserve it with one decisive dribble and the next pass.

title: Low-Man Rotation Rules
description: Teach the low man exactly when to tag, when to take the rim, and how the X-out finishes behind the play.
takeaway: Name the first rotator before you talk about the second.
answer_key: The low man protects the rim first and trusts the X-out behind him.

annotations.title: Early tag
annotations.note: The low man arrives before the pass, not after the catch.

annotations.title: Second rotator
annotations.note: The weak-side wing must already be moving to cover the low man's man.

annotations.title: Finish the possession
annotations.note: The final closeout is short and under control because the rotation started on time.

title: Timeout Usage Under Momentum Pressure
description: Separate emotional timeout calls from high-leverage timeout calls that actually change the possession quality.
takeaway: Use timeouts to fix the next two possessions, not just the last two mistakes.
answer_key: Use the timeout when the tactical issue is repeatable and the lineup needs a concrete reset.

scenario.prompt: Your team gave up back-to-back corner threes after the same rotation error. What is the best response?

options.title: Save the timeout and hope the players self-correct
options.description: You preserve resources but risk repeating the same mistake.

options.title: Call timeout, diagram the low-man responsibility, and change the weak-side matchup
options.description: You attack the repeated problem before the next possession.

options.title: Bench a scorer immediately without explaining the coverage breakdown
options.description: You send a message, but the coverage problem remains unclear.

scenario.explanation: The issue is structural, not emotional. Fix the repeated coverage and the lineup responsibility before play resumes.

title: After-Time-Out Play Sequencing
description: Build ATO packages that create one primary read and one clean counter instead of five average options.
takeaway: Clarity beats complexity when the clock matters.
answer_key: Sequence your first read and counter around your best two creators.

learn_more.title: Counter thinking
learn_more.body: Your second option should punish the exact scout adjustment the defense is most likely to make.

title: Value Creation Versus Raw Production
description: Learn why counting stats alone miss portability, defensive fit, and lineup elasticity in roster decisions.
takeaway: Skills that scale next to stars are worth more than empty volume.
answer_key: Separate volume from scalable impact when valuing a player.

title: When To Trade A Future First
description: Use timeline, surplus creation, and downside insulation to decide when moving a future first is actually rational.
takeaway: Trade picks when the move raises your real ceiling, not just your headline talent.
answer_key: A future first is expendable only when the current move materially improves the team's real contention path.

scenario.prompt: Your team won 49 games, has two star initiators, and a glaring playoff wing hole. Should you move a protected future first?

options.title: Yes, if the incoming wing solves a playoff-specific weakness and fits the stars
options.description: You are paying to fix a real postseason problem.

options.title: No, because future firsts should never be traded
options.description: This protects flexibility but ignores windows.

options.title: Yes, for any veteran scorer with name recognition
options.description: This chases optics rather than fit.

scenario.explanation: The question is not whether a first is valuable. It is whether the outgoing asset buys a real playoff upgrade with durable fit.

title: Coach Fit In The Front Office Process
description: Build coaching searches around the roster's constraints, development needs, and timeline instead of generic reputation.
takeaway: The right coach depends on the team you actually have.
answer_key: Hire toward the roster's next problem, not the coach's past brand.

pause_predict.prompt: A young roster ranks low in organization and defensive communication. Which coaching profile should the GM prioritize?

choices.label: A veteran motivator with little schematic reputation
A structure-first teacher with a track record building defensive habits
The biggest available name, regardless of fit

pause_predict.explanation: The roster's developmental need is structure. The hire should solve that need before it solves a branding problem.

title: Slot Cutting Versus Standing
description: Understand when a slot cut opens the paint for the driver and when holding spacing is the better decision.
takeaway: Movement has to create clarity, not clutter.
answer_key: Cut when the driver needs a passing lane or empty corner, not just because you are idle.

title: Transition Matchups Before Matchups
description: Teach defensive transition with rules that stop the ball and protect the rim before clean cross-matches are restored.
takeaway: Win the first two seconds, then sort out assignments.
answer_key: Sprint to ball and rim first, then trade back into preferred matchups.

title: Backup Center Or Fifth Shooter
description: Evaluate roster spots by playoff survivability rather than regular-season comfort.
takeaway: The twelfth man still matters if he changes your shape in May.
answer_key: The right marginal roster spot is the one that keeps your best lineup options alive.

scenario.prompt: A contender already has one trusted rim big. The last roster spot is between another traditional center and a corner-spacing wing. Which lens should decide it?

options.title: Pick the player who adds the most playoff lineup flexibility
options.description: You care about which option expands your closing groups.

options.title: Pick the player with the bigger per-game rebounding average
options.description: You reduce the decision to one regular-season stat.

options.title: Pick the player who is most comfortable staying on the bench
options.description: You optimize vibes over lineup value.

scenario.explanation: Marginal roster spots are about preserving lineup answers, especially in the playoffs.

title: Screen Angle Creates The Read
description: See how screen angle changes the defender's path and the handler's best read before the ball screen even lands.
takeaway: The advantage starts with the screen, not the dribble.
answer_key: A flipped angle changes where the help must come from and opens the next read.

annotations.title: Set the path
annotations.note: The screener's angle determines whether the defender can recover over the top.

annotations.title: Manipulate help
annotations.note: Once the angle changes, the low man becomes the next reader.

title: Short Roll Decision Ladder
description: Install a simple decision ladder for short-roll playmakers so every touch has a first, second, and third read.
takeaway: Structure the short roll before you celebrate it.
answer_key: Read rim, weak-side low man, then opposite slot.

pause_predict.prompt: The big catches on the short roll and the low man stays home. What is the next read?

choices.label: Spray to the opposite slot because the low man is locked to the dunker

pause_predict.explanation: If the low man stays attached, the opposite slot usually becomes the pressure-release pass.

title: Prospect Risk And Outcome Ranges
description: Grade prospects through expected outcomes, role probability, and developmental volatility instead of upside slogans.
takeaway: A wide range is not a flaw if your organization can absorb it.
answer_key: Your board should reflect both ceiling and the cost of missing on that archetype.

learn_more.title: Why range beats single-number grades
learn_more.body: Prospects do not arrive as a single median outcome. They arrive as development paths with different probabilities and costs.
